pageCache.text:
Our role is to support children who attend The Village School that have a diagnosis of a hearing, multi-sensory and/or visual impairment. This would be identified within their Educational Health and Care Plan.
We support through ‘in class’ teaching which allows us to help provide strategies that best support our hearing, multi-sensory and vision impairment children’s learning. As a team we also support children in smaller groups or focus sessions, depending on their level of need.
As a school, we work closely with Seeability and specialist hospitals. Please click on SeeAbility link below for more information about this service.
We also have links with the Audiology clinic and the cochlear implant centres for our students.
Parents are invited to telephone the school office if they wish to make an appointment to discuss their child’s vision, hearing or sensory impairments

Inclusion

Teaching and interventions are evaluated for impact and adapted swiftly to meet pupils’ emerging needs.

Pupils, including past pupils, should have meaningful access to opportunities within the local and wider community.
Research, innovation and high‑quality professional development are at the heart of how we support pupils to achieve their best.
Families and communities are an integral part of The Village School we work as a team, uphold our shared values and welcome collaboration with our partners

Welcome to The Village School
It takes a village to raise a child
Welcome to The Village School
It is a pleasure to welcome you to The Village School, a specialist setting in the London Borough of Brent dedicated to supporting children and young people with a wide range of skills, abilities and unique talents.
We are a vibrant and nurturing learning community made up of five villages, serving pupils aged 3 to 19. With an enrolment of 310 students, we are united by a clear purpose: to ensure every learner is recognised, valued and empowered to flourish.
Our Curriculum and Approach
Our curriculum is designed as a progress model, enabling every young person to be an active and enthusiastic participant in their learning journey. We nurture curiosity, independence and a joy for learning, ensuring all students are encouraged to explore, grow and experience the fullness of life both within and beyond school.
At the heart of our curriculum is a commitment to personal progress, high aspirations and inclusion. We believe every child deserves the opportunity to achieve their best, in a school where they feel seen, supported and inspired.
Our Values
At The Village School, our values are rooted in a commitment to progress, attainment, inclusion, and principled practice. We believe that every learner deserves the opportunity to grow, achieve and participate fully in school life.
These values are brought to life through our curriculum, which is designed to support each student’s needs and aspirations. It promotes engagement, enjoyment, confidence and the development of essential life-skills, helping every young person make meaningful progress.
We foster a strong sense of belonging, where all students are welcomed, understood and celebrated. Our community is built on kindness, respect, appreciation and effective communication, ensuring positive relationships and a safe, nurturing environment for all.
We work intentionally to create a culture where:
These values shape everyday practice across our five villages, enabling each young person to develop confidence, independence and a deep sense of selfâ€‘worth.
Kindness and respect guide expectations and interactions.
Working in Partnership
We know that the best outcomes are achieved through strong collaboration. Parents, Carers and Guardians are central to our work. We work closely with families and multiâ€‘professional teams to ensure that every learner’s journey is purposeful, personalised and joyful, always with an unrelenting focus on preparing young people for the next stage in life.
Our Sites
The Village School operates across three sites:
The Village School (Main Site): 29 classes
The Hope Centre: 2 classes
Our Community
All students at The Village School have an Education, Health and Care Plan, and many have additional complex medical needs or a diagnosis of Autism. Our school reflects the rich diversity of Brent, with pupils from a variety of cultural, ethnic and faith backgrounds. The proportion of learners supported through Pupil Premium is higher than the national average.
We truly believe that every child can shine. Through a transdisciplinary approach and a curriculum rich in communication, independence, creativity and physical development, we provide enriching opportunities that prepare each learner for a confident, meaningful and empowered adult life.
A Final Word
At The Village School, we see potential in every child and we are relentless in helping them realise it. Together with our families, staff and community partners, we create a place where young people feel proud of who they are, excited about who they can become, and ready to take their next steps with courage, joy and hope.
Welcome to The Village School. Welcome to our community.
Jurita Bennett Head of School The Village School
Ofsted 2023 - "Outstanding"
Don’t Worry About a Thing
It’s a hot Tuesday afternoon. Imagine this. It’s school council time. A bright, spacious, vibrant room opens its doors to a kaleidoscope of ways to be heard, to speak. Here, we listen with our eyes.
It’s a special school in north-west London. The classroom is full. Thirty young people, some ambulant, others profoundly dependent, all luminous in their own way. The room hums with joyful noise: a cacophony, yes, but a constructive one – a choir of movement, sound, and delight.
Teaching assistants,120% attentive, move with practised grace, responding not just to need but to personality. They know every child. Every tick, twitch, sign, and smile. We’re signing the words to Three Little Birds. Bob Marley fills the air.
To our surprise, a boy who barely moves shouts a single word: ‘Marley’. The room bursts into applause. Nearby, another child bounces from chair to chair – their connections to people, to books, to life itself run deep. They weren’t always understood. But the adults in that child’s family kept going. Their investment in their child matched the school’s commitment to them. Valued attention that ran both ways. The school helped turn frustration into calm, assertive advocacy.
This school sees that child. They understand them. And they make sure others do too.
The session ends, but the mood lingers. Before leaving, we all sign the three words these pupils know by heart – happy, love, fun.
Because here, at last, they are.
Challenge Partner Lead Inspector

Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA)
Strengthening School–Family Partnerships
At The Village School, we believe that children achieve their very best when schools and families work together. That is why we are proud to be working towards the Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA) — a nationally recognised accreditation celebrating outstanding parental engagement in schools.
The LPPA helps us build even stronger relationships with parents and carers, ensuring that your voice, involvement and partnership remain central to our school community.
What Is the LPPA?
The Leading Parent Partnership Award is a structured framework that supports schools in developing high-quality, meaningful engagement with parents. It focuses on strengthening communication, improving participation and creating opportunities for parents to play an active role in their child’s learning.
By working towards this award, we are:
Identifying opportunities for improvement
Committing to ongoing, community-informed development
Why It Matters
Research shows that strong home–school relationships have a significant positive impact on:
We want every family to feel connected, informed and empowered to be part of their child’s journey.
Children’s progress and attainment
Confidence, well-being and behaviour
Attendance and punctuality
Longâ€‘term learning habits and independence
Our LPPA Priorities
As part of the LPPA process, we are strengthening our approach across nine key areas, including:
Ensuring the school is welcoming and approachable
Providing clear, accessible communication for all families
Supporting parents during induction and transitions
Celebrating parental involvement and success
How Parents Can Get Involved
Your involvement is vital to our success. Throughout the year we will be offering:
Workshops & Learning Events
Handsâ€‘on activities that help you support learning at home and understand what your child experiences in school.
Parent Focus Groups & Surveys
Opportunities to share your ideas, feedback and experiences.
Family Celebrations & Community Events
Moments to come together as a school community, celebrating strengths and successes.
Volunteering & Project Groups
Parents and carers who want to become more involved in specific aspects of school life are always welcome.
What’s Happening Now
We are currently completing our LPPA selfâ€‘evaluation and developing our action plan. This work builds on our existing strengths, including the growing focus on community engagement which is noted in our School Development Plan and marks ongoing progress towards LPPA and highlights parent partnership as an important strategic priority.
We will continue sharing updates, celebrating successes and inviting parent participation as we progress.
We Want to Hear From You
Your views matter. If you have suggestions, ideas or questions about the LPPA or parent engagement more generally, please get in touch with us. Together, we can continue building a school community where every child and family feels fully supported.

Strengthening School–Family Partnerships
At The Village School, we believe that children achieve their very best when schools and families work together. That is why we are proud to be working towards the Leading Parent Partnership Award (LPPA) — a nationally recognised accreditation celebrating outstanding parental engagement in schools.
The LPPA helps us build even stronger relationships with parents and carers, ensuring that your voice, involvement and partnership remain central to our school community.
What Is the LPPA?
The Leading Parent Partnership Award is a structured framework that supports schools in developing high-quality, meaningful engagement with parents. It focuses on strengthening communication, improving participation and creating opportunities for parents to play an active role in their child’s learning.
By working towards this award, we are:
Identifying opportunities for improvement
Committing to ongoing, community-informed development
Why It Matters
Research shows that strong home–school relationships have a significant positive impact on:
We want every family to feel connected, informed and empowered to be part of their child’s journey.
Children’s progress and attainment
Confidence, well-being and behaviour
Attendance and punctuality
Longâ€‘term learning habits and independence
Our LPPA Priorities
As part of the LPPA process, we are strengthening our approach across nine key areas, including:
Ensuring the school is welcoming and approachable
Providing clear, accessible communication for all families
Supporting parents during induction and transitions
Celebrating parental involvement and success

Your involvement is vital to our success. Throughout the year we will be offering:

Parents and carers who want to become more involved in specific aspects of school life are always welcome.
What’s Happening Now
We are currently completing our LPPA selfâ€‘evaluation and developing our action plan. This work builds on our existing strengths, including the growing focus on community engagement which is noted in our School Development Plan and marks ongoing progress towards LPPA and highlights parent partnership as an important strategic priority.
We will continue sharing updates, celebrating successes and inviting parent participation as we progress.

Challenge Partners’ Quality Assurance Review
Challenge Partners’ quality assurance is built around the QA Review, a professionally-led peer review focused on teaching and learning. The review identifies areas of strength and development, bringing key challenges to schools for the coming year and providing Continuing Professional Development (CPDL) for all participants. It is a joint exercise between the review team and the school. All activities include a member of the school working alongside the reviewers.
Our recent Challenge Partners Review took place in June 2025.
Challenge Partners Review June 2025
Challenge Partners Review Report January 2023 Challenge Partners Review Report February 2022
Challenge Partners Review Report June 2021
Don’t Worry About a Thing
It’s a hot Tuesday afternoon. Imagine this. It’s school council time. A bright, spacious, vibrant room opens its doors to a kaleidoscope of ways to be heard, to speak. Here, we listen with our eyes.
It’s a special school in north-west London. The classroom is full. Thirty young people, some ambulant, others profoundly dependent, all luminous in their own way. The room hums with joyful noise: a cacophony, yes, but a constructive one – a choir of movement, sound, and delight.
Teaching assistants,120% attentive, move with practised grace, responding not just to need but to personality. They know every child. Every tick, twitch, sign, and smile. We’re signing the words to Three Little Birds. Bob Marley fills the air.
To our surprise, a boy who barely moves shouts a single word: ‘Marley’. The room bursts into applause. Nearby, another child bounces from chair to chair – their connections to people, to books, to life itself run deep. They weren’t always understood. But the adults in that child’s family kept going. Their investment in their child matched the school’s commitment to them. Valued attention that ran both ways. The school helped turn frustration into calm, assertive advocacy.
This school sees that child. They understand them. And they make sure others do too.
The session ends, but the mood lingers. Before leaving, we all sign the three words these pupils know by heart – happy, love, fun.
Because here, at last, they are.

Mission Statement: The Village School is dedicated to providing inclusive, nurturing education for children with special educational needs and disabilities. Our school community spans five unique "villages"—Primary, Main School, Kay Charles Village, Kingsbury Village, and Hope Village—each contributing to a diverse and vibrant learning environment. At the heart of our mission is the belief that our students' educational journeys can be continually enriched, both within our classrooms and in the wider spaces around our school.
Our Purpose: As the PTA, our goal is to enhance every aspect of our school environment to support the sensory, academic, and developmental needs of our exceptional learners. We also aim to build a strong sense of community engagement, ensuring that all students, families, and staff feel a shared commitment to growth and inclusion.
Meetings and Involvement: Our PTA committee, formed just last year, meets in school every other month, providing a welcoming space for collaboration and planning. We encourage new staff and parents to join us, either as committee members or as part of our Steering Group. Our next Annual General Meeting will be held on Wednesday, December 4 2024, and all interested are invited to attend!
Get in Touch: We’d love to welcome you to the PTA! Whether you’d like to join, pledge support, or simply learn more about our work and fundraising activities, please reach out to us at: friendsofthevillage@compasslp.co.uk.
Upcoming Events: After the fantastic success of our Summer Fête this year, we’re excited to host another in 2025! We’re also planning a cozy seasonal day for our staff and children and a festive raffle. Additionally, we’ll be holding a clothes-swapping event for parents and staff, complete with tea, cake, and a warm welcome.
Our Achievements So Far: Since forming last year, the PTA has successfully raised funds to support valuable additions to our school, including a beautiful play kitchenette for our primary students. This resource enhances their "Preparation for Adulthood" curriculum by encouraging learning through play. We are also thrilled to announce that we can now purchase specialised tables for our art classes, making them more accessible to our PMLD (Profound and Multiple Learning Disabilities) learners.

The Village School seeks to maximise the life chances of all our young people and prepare them for life beyond school and college.

The Village School Expressive Arts Curriculum Overview A big emphasis is placed on the Expressive Arts at The Village School as it is an area in which our pupils over time have achieved very successful outcomes, both in terms of formal qualifications and also with regards to self-esteem, communication, behaviour, independence and developing self-expression.
At The Village, we take the view that ALL children can enjoy and achieve in the arts and that all children should have equal access to arts opportunities no matter what their style of learning or baseline assessment may be.
We have high expectations of success and frequently see children exceeding expectations. We teach the arts so that our pupils can become skilled practitioners in art, music, drama and dance. We also recognise that through this teaching other transferable skills are gained, such as social interaction, communication and the ability to behave appropriately and learn independently.
The arts subjects are linked to other learning in the school through following the whole school curriculum theme-based learning for each term.
Provision Every pupil at The Village has music and art lessons throughout the year taught by a specialist. Throughout their time at school they also have access to drama and dance lessons with a specialist for a period of time. Lessons, which include off-site learning at galleries and concert halls as well as in our linked mainstream schools, culminate in performances and exhibitions both in and out of school so that children have the experience of sharing their achievements with others in and beyond the community. Arts lessons follow the Stepping Stones, Tracks and Lanes pathways for personalised learning. Themes are adapted to work in multi-sensory ways with children on the Stepping Stones pathway. Lessons are differentiated to embed progress, inclusion and entitlement for all.
Assessment, recording and Accreditations The Village School is dedicated to monitoring the impact of our arts provision. We do this by offering a vast array of accreditations in the arts as well as having strong assessment and recording procedures in place.
Progression As pupils progress through the Key Stages, age appropriate learning is ensured and progression maintained through the schemes of work. For example, Village 1 children follow early Years and Foundation Stage principles with exploratory learning through play and games and in Key Stage 5 there is formal accreditation linked to outside partnerships with organisations which can provide future work and leisure opportunities.
Communication/Accessibility All teachers of the arts liaise routinely with the multi-disciplinary team of professionals at The Village School and visiting arts professionals are advised of our range of communication systems. In addition to this the arts themselves, at the Village School, have been shown to provide a vehicle for communication and self-expression at the deepest level. There is also joint working with the Occupational Therapists and the Positive Behaviour Inclusion team to ensure safety, progress and inclusion in all arts lessons.
Partnerships for improvement The arts curriculum at The Village School is enriched by its links and partnerships with a big variety of the learning departments of galleries, concert halls and theatre groups as well as through our arts links in our two linked mainstream schools. Research into improving curriculum planning and assessment methods is ongoing through a partnership with Roehampton University.
Live Music Now Partnership
Live Music Now (LMN) collaborated with Media Trust and filmmaker Tyro Heath to capture the importance of music to children with additional learning needs.
The result is a moving insight into the positive effects of music. The featured project took place at The Village School in Brent and is part of LMN’s Inspire programme – providing enriching and inclusive music provision in special schools, led by professional musicians from Live Music Now.

pageCache.pageTitle: PE & Rebound Therapy - The Village School
pageCache.text:
Curriculum Intent & Implementation.
Physical Education at The Village School offers a broad, balanced, and sequenced curriculum that ensures progress and accessibility for all learners, promoting physical development, well-being, and inclusion through diverse, therapeutic, and competitive opportunities.
Our curriculum goes beyond weekly lessons, offering inclusive activities, external partnerships, and real-world opportunities for learners to develop skills, gain qualifications, and thrive. Led by skilled staff, our diverse and therapeutic program is tailored to meet the individual needs of our learners.
Multisport Activities: A wide range of sports are offered in our sports hall and outdoor spaces, encouraging teamwork, motor skills, and enjoyment.
Rebound Therapy: Delivered by certified staff, this approach uses trampolining to support movement, balance, muscle tone regulation, relaxation, sensory integration, and communication. It is particularly beneficial for learners with physical disabilities and is supported by our Occupational Therapy and Physical Management teams.
Aquatic Therapy and Swimming: learners access swimming and water-based therapy sessions in our on-site swimming pool, heated to a temperature that facilitates hydrotherapy sessions, promoting fitness, coordination, relaxation, the acquisition of aquatic skills, and confidence in the water.
Enrichment and External Partnerships
We are proud to collaborate with a number of outstanding organisations to extend our PE offer beyond the school gates:
Willesden Sports Centre Access: Sixth form learners attend weekly PE at the local sports hall, while learners at the Kingsbury Village site benefit from swimming lessons tailored to their needs. These off-site sessions promote skill development, independence, community engagement, and preparation for adulthood.
Panathlon Competitions: Our learners from Key Stages 2-5 have the opportunity to participate in multisport and swimming competitions designed for young people with disabilities, encouraging achievement and inclusion.
Snowbility: Provide adaptive skiing experiences that allow our learners to build confidence and physical skills in a fun and challenging environment. Our learners follow bespoke, accredited assessments to track their progress; some learners' work contributes to their Duke of Edinburgh Bronze Award, whilst one of our learners gained a scholarship and the possibility of employment.
Middlesex FA SEN Schools League: Our learners participate in inclusive weekly football fixtures against other local schools, giving them the chance to develop and express their football skills while building teamwork, sportsmanship and social skills, embedding themselves into the broader community.
Bloomsbury Football Foundation Festivals: These events offer learners the opportunity to participate in structured football activities alongside peers and other schools, led by expert coaches. We have been fortunate to gain access to Premier League football stadiums and training facilities through this partnership.
Stoke Mandeville National Junior Games: Our annual residential trip to the birthplace of the Paralympic Games provides our learners with opportunities to take part in disability multi-sport events where they compete and celebrate their abilities, accessing the latest and most innovative disability sports equipment.
National Sports Week: We celebrate this annual event with a week’s sports festival culminating in a whole school closing ceremony event to celebrate each class's participation and success
Hendon Football Club:Through our collaboration with Hendon FC, learners and their families can attend complimentary live matches at Silver Jubilee Park. Many learners have earned 1st4Sport Level 1 and 2 coaching qualifications and returned to deliver coaching to their peers. They also use Hendon’s facilities for interschool matches, including games with partner schools from the Middlesex SEN Schools League.
Through these collaborations, we actively promote social inclusion and inspire the empowerment of our young people at The Village School.

pageCache.text:
Learning at home is a broad term to describe the learning which happens without the school. It can take place through everyday activities including play and general family life, such as food preparation and cooking. It can also happen through curriculum-related activities, homework, reading and sharing books.
The TVS class teachers will provide activities for learning at home that will be specifically designed to help parents engage in their child’s learning and build upon the learning from the schools. You will find appropriate resources in the class folders and on this website. Please review our Staying Safe On Line pointers below, which will help you and your family get the most out of the internet safely.
Engaging in your child’s learning can make a real difference in how well they do. Making your home a positive home learning environment plays a big part in this, no matter what age and skills your child has.
The Village Teachers and class teams have all contributed useful websites and activities to these pages, to help you with home schooling when needed.
We've split up the resources so that there is a collection of resources, whatever pathway your child is on. Use the links below or on the left to view the resources for each pathway. Please also review the General Resources page for relevant material across all pathways.
If you are unsure of the pathway for your child, or you'd like some suggested activities for your child, please contact a member of your child's class team.
Staying Safe On Line Broadband, mobile and WiFi providers offer filters to limit the inappropriate content a child might see. As these typically have to be set manually, you’ll find a comprehensive list of parental control guides on the Internet Matters website, or call your internet provider for assistance. For parental controls, which allow you to you to determine what sites and apps your child can access with their smartphone, tablet or laptop, there are several paid options, but Google's Family Link is the most comprehensive, and it's free. It also lets you set limits on how long a child can spend on their device and even allow you to monitor exactly how they’re using it. Parental controls can take care of the possibility of children running up expensive bills, by letting you set spending limits. Or you can set up your child’s phone so they can’t spend any money at all. Remember that no filter or parental controls tool is 100% effective, and many of the risks that young people face online are because of their own and other’s behaviour. It is therefore important to talk to your children about staying safe online, encourage good behaviour and make sure they know that they can turn to you if they get into any difficulty. The ThinkYouKnow guide is a useful set of things to consider in addition to filters and controls
We recommend resources such as Internet Matters, The UK Safer Internet Centre, Parent Zone, Think You Know and the NSPCC as excellent places to find advice for developing good habits and keeping your child safe whilst on the internet Don't forget, if children are taking their devices out of the home, it's worth bearing in mind that they could connect to public wifi, for example, in a shop, cafe or restaurant. Look out for the Friendly WiFi symbol which shows that the wifi has filters in place.

Wellbeing Awareness
Wellbeing' refers to a state of positive mental health and wellness..
It involves a sense of optimism, confidence, happiness, clarity, vitality, self-worth, achievement, having a meaning and purpose, engagement, having supportive and satisfying relationships with others and understanding oneself, and responding effectively to one’s own emotions.
At the Village School, early intervention and a whole school approach can be highly effective in improving wellbeing and reducing the impact of mental health problems. This whole school and community approach involves parents as well.
Wellbeing & Support Provision Map
Explore our interactive Wellbeing & Support Provision Map to discover the wide range of help. This easy-to-use tool guides you to the right support—whether you’re looking for general advice, targeted group support, or specialist services. You can quickly find information about in-school resources as well as external organisations, ensuring everyone in our community can access the assistance they need.
City and Mental Health Alliance Toolkit
The toolkit provide an overview of the key topics dealing with mental health, signposts you to further information from trusted sources, and shares insights from parents and young people who have been through it. This toolkit will help you to:
Mental Health Awareness Week The Mental Health Foundation gives practical steps to help you address the issues regarding mental health and well being, focusing on loneliness
Well Being and Cost of Living Assistance With the cost of living increasing and winter almost upon us, things might feel a bit uncertain and worrying. Above is a link that has some helpful resources, particularly during this time, from financial support to looking after your mental health. We hope you find this useful.
Young Minds is a UK charity for children and young people's mental health.
Place2Be is a UK children's mental health charity.
Mind is the UK’s leading mental health charity, offering a great deal of useful information on children’s mental health.
Children's Mental Health Week is an annual opportunity to encourage children, young people and adults to celebrate their uniqueness.
Children and young people’s mental health services (CYPMHS; sometimes also known by its older name Child and Adolescent Mental Health Services (CAMHS)) are funded by the NHS to provide support to children and young people with a wide range of behavioural and emotional issues.
NHS children's mental health provides ways to support young people with mental health problems.
The Children’s Commissioner provides advice and government reports on mental health and wellbeing.

School - Family Communication
The Village school values parent, carer, and family partnerships. We do this carefully in four ways:
1. Open Communication: Families receive their child’s targets, timetables, medium-term planning aims, proactive support plans, and class team updates each term. The school promotes communication that values working together, celebrating successes, and problem-solving with the solution as the aim. The best way to contact us is via email or phone.
Telephone: 0300 303 0610
E-mail Address: TVS-Office@compasslp.co.uk
2. Evidence for Learning: The school uses the online system Evidence for Learning. Every family has a protected login into the system. Families regularly receive updates on their child’s learning. This is to build the picture of progress. Families are invited to share key experiences in the home environment so that class teams can learn and incorporate this into the class planning.
(CLICK for more information)
3. Arbor App: The Arbor Parent App is our chosen Parent App for managing pupil and parent information. We are now using the ‘Arbor App’ for almost all we do alongside email.
We are still developing how Arbor is used in this way, and the breadth of what can be accessed from within the app will only expand over time.
(CLICK for more information)
4. Parent Forum & Feedback:
We welcome feedback from parents and carers as we believe it enables us to better support our students. We also survey parents, carers, staff, and students every year to make sure they are listening to everyone in our community.
Each term we host an Online and in-person Parent Forum which will share a short presentation about a pre-publicised topic, e.g. exams & assessments or personal development, followed by the opportunity for parents/carers to ask Mr Stelamszczyk (Headteacher) any questions on any topic.

Brent SEND Newsletter, Issue 14 Jul 2025
A single place to come for information and advice for children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) aged 0-25, and their families.
Please check the link below to access the relevant information
SEND Local Offer | Brent Council
You’ll find everything from activities, to information explaining the support available to you and your child and where to go for independent advice.
To use the Local Offer choose from a range of information and advice.
Find out: What SEND is, what to do if you think your child has SEND, getting an assessment of your child’s needs and how support can change to meet those needs.
Information, support and advice: Find the right school in Brent, information on health services, the range of support and advice out there, help with travel and transport needs, financial support and more.
Things to do: A directory of things to do, including sporting activities, clubs and hobbies and short respite breaks.
2. Brent Parent Carer Forum
Brent Parent Carer Forum offers information, support and friendship for families of children and young people aged 0-25 with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND). We are the strategic voice of parent carers 0-25 living in Brent.
-we provide opportunities to meet together with other parents to share lived experiences
-we provide support to parents to access information and how to navigate the right services
-we run consultation and information monthly sessions 1 day time 1 evening
-we are parent-led and independent
-we are the official strategy the voice and the critical friend of health, education, and social care services in Brent
- working in partnership
To become a member Become a member – BRENT PARENT CARERS CIC (brentpcf.org)
To contact us email admin@brentpcf.org or call 07305145167 and leave a message.
3. Brent Carers
Brent Carers Centre offer carers living in, or caring for a person living in, Brent an extensive range of information and advice services on all aspects of their caring responsibilities, via the operation of the Brent Carers Services Hub and other local initiatives.
http://www.brentcarerscentre.org.uk/
4. Brent Mencap
Is a charity to support people with a learning disability.
http://www.brentmencap.org.uk/
5. Brent Parent Partnership
Offers independent, confidential advice to the parents or carer’s of children who have special educational needs.
Email: parentpartnership@brent.gov.uk
6. Resources for Autism
Provide practical services for children and adults with an autistic spectrum condition and for their families and carers.
http://www.resourcesforautism.org.uk/
7. BOAT
The Brent outreach autism team works with children and young people who have been diagnosed on the autism spectrum. The service they provide is mostly school based with some advice and support offered to families. We support all children and young people at mainstream Brent schools, including sixth-forms, whether they live in the borough or not.
http://brent.gov.uk/boat
8. ADHD and Autism Support Harrow
autism@adhdandautismharrow.co.uk
9. “Family Fund”
Are the UK’s largest provider of grants to low-income families raising disabled and seriously ill children and young people. They help ease the additional pressures families face.
http://www.familyfund.org.uk/
10. NAS – Ladbroke Grove resource (website)
Ladbroke Grove Autism Centre supports people of all ages on the autism spectrum to help them achieve their full potential. They offer a safe and supportive environment in which children, young people and adults can meet other people, try new activities, explore interests and develop their confidence and independence.
